data.long_meaning: Abel (הֶבֶל) is a name of Hebrew origin meaning “Breath; vapour; transitory; that which is fleeting”. From Hebrew הֶבֶל (hevel) 'breath, vapour, that which is transitory', from the verb הבל (habal). The same word underlies the refrain 'vanity of vanities' in Ecclesiastes. A cognate of Akkadian ablu 'son' has also been proposed. Its root is Hebrew הֶבֶל (hevel), from the verb הבל (habal) 'to act emptily, become vain'. Abel is the anglicised form of Biblical Hebrew Hevel. It is distinct from Abel (place name אָבֵל 'meadow', 2 Samuel 20:14) - a distinct Hebrew word.

faq.q: What does the name Abel mean?
faq.a: Abel means “Breath; vapour; transitory; that which is fleeting”.

faq.q: What is the etymology of Abel?
faq.a: From Hebrew הֶבֶל (hevel) 'breath, vapour, that which is transitory', from the verb הבל (habal). The same word underlies the refrain 'vanity of vanities' in Ecclesiastes. A cognate of Akkadian ablu 'son' has also been proposed.

faq.q: Does Abel appear in the Bible?
faq.a: Yes. The personal name occurs in Genesis and is referenced in the New Testament (Matthew 23:35; Hebrews 11:4).

faq.q: Is Abel a Biblical name?
faq.a: Yes — the personal name occurs in the Biblical text. The personal name occurs in Genesis and is referenced in the New Testament (Matthew 23:35; Hebrews 11:4).

faq.q: Does Abel occur in the Old Testament?
faq.a: Yes.

faq.q: Does Abel occur in the New Testament?
faq.a: Yes.

faq.q: Is Abel associated with a saint?
faq.a: No saint association is verified for the name Abel.

faq.q: Is the meaning of Abel verified?
faq.a: The meaning “Breath; vapour; transitory; that which is fleeting” is supported by Old Testament: Abel, second son of Adam and Eve, killed by Cain (Genesis 4:2-8). Confidence: HIGH.

faq.q: What is the numerology or lucky number of Abel?
faq.a: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Abel total 20, reducing to 2. Number 2 is traditionally associated with cooperation, balance and sensitivity. This is an interpretive tradition, not a factual claim.

faq.q: What are the common spelling variants of Abel?
faq.a: Variants and alternative forms include Hevel, Abelardo (unrelated).

faq.q: Is Abel the same as Abel?
faq.a: No. Abel is distinct from Abel (place name אָבֵל 'meadow', 2 Samuel 20:14) - a distinct Hebrew word.

faq.q: What is the transliteration of Abel?
faq.a: Abel is transliterated as Hevel.

faq.q: How many syllables does Abel have?
faq.a: Abel has 2 syllables.

faq.q: What are the spiritual connotations of Abel?
faq.a: Any spiritual significance attached to Abel is interpretive. Its documented core is the lexical meaning “Breath; vapour; transitory; that which is fleeting”, and readings built on that meaning are presented as tradition rather than as religious doctrine.

faq.q: Where is the name Abel used today?
faq.a: Abel circulates chiefly in Biblical Hebrew, English, Greek, Latin naming communities. No verified registration statistics are published for it.
